description: The sleep band is 66 F floor / 68 F ceiling. The +4 F cap would allow 70 F, but heating never goes above the comfort band's ceiling: only ONE 2 F step (68 F) is allowed and the bedroom stays cold rather than the loop crossing the opposite edge.

events.note: The hallway thermostat's own sensor: satisfied, so it will not start by itself.
Day classification (cold: heat all night / hot: cool all night).
Bedtime: the sleep band is written and the sleep window (remote sensor in use) begins.

assertions.reason: With a sleep ceiling of 68 F and a 66 F target only 2 F of room exists: ONE step, then nothing, although the +4 F cap would allow 70 and the bedroom is still cold.
Heating never above the comfort band's ceiling.

notes: Three-exercise protocol (CLAUDE.md section 10), Issue #1194 increment (e). Tier A: the real ClimateAdvisorCoordinator + AutomationEngine under FakeHass/FakeScheduler (use_coordinator=true, so the sleep-sensor listener and the 1-minute timer are real); every assertion is track=integration for that reason and is evaluated, not skipped.

(a) Effectiveness: scratch-copy mutation run of this scenario against the production code (worktree untouched). It FAILS when M01: the whole offset deleted (the write path adds 0 and the check is a no-op); M03: the opposite-band-edge cap ignored. Passes unmutated.

(b) Docs <-> production alignment: docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md 'Remote-sensor outer loop on the thermostat setpoint (Issue #1194, increment a)': 'Caps (the tighter wins)' and remote_offset.max_magnitude_f. Matches production.
(c) Occupant outcome if this regressed: Crossing the opposite edge makes the band re-resolution (time of day, TOU) fight the loop and thrash the setpoint all night.

verdict.summary: The opposite-edge cap wins over the +4 F cap when it is tighter (heat).
verdict.observed_behavior: Writes: 66, 68, then none for two hours.
verdict.expected_behavior: The tighter of the +4 F cap and the opposite band edge wins.
